definition: knowing my own feeling the way I would know a stranger's, by deduction

settled:
Almost all my emotional understanding of myself is deduction rather than feeling.

I relate to my own emotional life the way other people relate to somebody else's. I read the behaviour and work the feeling back out of it. My own heart is a thing I study, the way I would study a person sitting across the table from me.

The will to live is the sharp end of it. It sits in the tenth of me I cannot read, so I cannot know it is there. I catch it when it leaks past the surface and reason backwards from the leak.

Building one of my personas, I watched myself start to cry and read the tears as a will to live I had not known I had. Asked what the tears felt like, I had nothing to answer with. There was no stored feeling to replay.

So the most fundamental thing about being alive is, for me, the least directly visible, and I hold it by probability rather than by certainty.

title: Studying My Own Heart From Outside
